volume.author: spec-author seat, group G5 Owner surface, round 1

contents.entry: Mechanism: Intake.Answer and the one-ruling rule
The sources of an answer, and which effects each may carry
How it starts without an agent typing
Every wait, its timeout and its fallback
State paths and their cleanup scripts

pointers.sibling: JSON schema of owner.answer and ruling
Bearings page service: the owner's answer leaves the page here
Controls screen: control.action enters as an owner action
Watcher: the second deliverer of every answer
Card builder: the ruling closes the card
Flags: the single writer of flag:hold and flag:build_mode, which applies this node's typed effects
Inbox: an owner word typed on the owner page arrives as an answer on its standing card
Ticket intake: a ruling that unblocks a dead ticket
pointers.shared: Who may relay an owner answer
Owner words: whole trimmed message from an owner principal
Relayable and defaultable effects: none and ticket.unblock only
The caller's node, by and role come from SO_PEERCRED, never from the request
Where this node goes live in the one cut-over order of the book

purpose.is: The intake turns the owner's pick and words on a card into one ruling record in the store that every gate and cut-over node reads, with exactly one ruling per card id, whoever delivers it and however many times.
purpose.is-not: It never interprets the words, never decides for the owner, and never types anything into an agent.
purpose.why: Today an answer is a line in answers.jsonl read by one wait loop and typed into one pane (L08 finding 1); a relayed answer from chat (C42, "went recommended", recorded by hand) had no system path; and rulings that a gate checks were sometimes unrecorded (memory rulings-gates-check-are-records: PR 156 reworked). A ruling is a record or it did not happen.
purpose.decisions: D12 system lane (C40), D15 the owner holds the line through cards (C50), D10 one store (C34), no-bureaucracy-creep (an answer given where the owner is, recorded as the card's answer), rulings-gates-check-are-records.

input.text: The record arrives by gRPC Intake.Answer from the page service (N-32) in the same request as the owner's tap, from the watcher (N-27) as the second deliverer of a record already persisted, from the inbox (N-30) for an owner word typed on the page, from the owner CLI (coq owner answer, or --relay), from the standing policy at a deadline (N-28), or from the Controls screen (N-42, through N-32) as a control.action answered on its standing card. All are the same record kind with a different source.

typed, one object per effect (record.schema.json#/$defs/effect): ticket.unblock {ticket}; build-mode.set {state, scope, expires_at, card_id} and control.halt or control.resume {card_id, word} as nodes/N-44/record.schema.json#/$defs/flag_effect defines them; gofactory {card_id}; break.glass {request, target}; promotion.confirm {head_sha}; none

output.text: The ruling is immutable. One ruling per card: operation key N-29/ruling/<card_id>/r1 (shared/contracts.xml#operation-keys) and the entity ruling:<card_id> created with expected version 0, in one commit. A standing card (nodes/N-28/spec.xml#standing-cards) is answered once per action: N-29/ruling/<card_id>@<action_id>/r1 and entity ruling:<card_id>@<action_id>. A repeat of the same answer replays the ruling (200); a different answer to an answered card is answer.refused 409 with the existing ruling attached, and the page shows "already answered: <choice> at <at>" as an ack. The gates and cut-over nodes (N-44, N-49, N-50, N-03) tail ruling records and read effects.

record.field: the card; the existing ruling id; shown to the owner as an ack

400: unknown card, pick out of range, card not open on this tier, words over cap, not a standing card (an inbox or Controls answer on an ordinary card); 403: not_relayable (a relayed, defaulted or imported answer whose effect is owner-only, shared/authority.xml#relayable-rulings), not_owner (an owner-only effect from a principal that is not the owner, a viewer session among them), caller_not_allowed (a caller outside the permissions section for that source)
not-ready: a USERGO (control.resume) before bootstrap state B7, naming the missing proofs (shared/cut-over.xml#bootstrap); no ruling is written and the standing card stays open

mechanism.where: Go service (D01), package internal/owner/intake, gRPC service Intake with one method Answer(AnswerRequest) returns (AnswerReply) on /run/coq/store.sock, authenticated by SO_PEERCRED (shared/authority.xml#peer-credentials); its callers are the permissions section's list and nothing else.
mechanism.step: Validate: the card record exists, is on the named tier, has no card.done (a standing card never has one); pick is within its options; words under the cap; action_id present exactly when the card is a standing card. Authority, from the server-derived principal and the caller's node, never from a request field: each source has its allowed callers (permissions section); an owner-only effect (anything but none and ticket.unblock) needs principal_role owner and source page, controls or cli (shared/authority.xml#owner-words), else answer.rejected 403 not_relayable or not_owner; a relayed, defaulted or imported answer may carry only none or ticket.unblock (shared/authority.xml#relayable-rulings). A control.resume before bootstrap B7 is control.refused 412 not-ready naming the missing proofs. Every refusal is returned in the reply and written as a record so the page can show it and the health line can count it.

Persist the owner.answer record first under operation key N-29/owner.answer/<answer id>/r1 (a repeat replays the stored record), so the owner's act is never lost even if the next step fails. This is V16's "persisted before acknowledged" carried into the store.

Rule: one Store.Commit with operation key N-29/ruling/<card_id>/r1 (standing card: N-29/ruling/<card_id>@<action_id>/r1) that creates the entity ruling:<card_id> (or ruling:<card_id>@<action_id>) at expected version 0 and appends the ruling record. A replay with the same request hash returns the ruling (200); a version conflict or idempotency_mismatch (409) means another answer ruled first: return answer.refused 409 with that ruling. Imported answers are ruled with effects [none] and are never matched to a live card's effect.

Effects are typed and computed by a rule table (tools/bearings/config/answer-effects.json, keyed on the card's template row and the pick), then filtered by step 1's authority: a pick that unblocks a dead ticket is ticket.unblock {ticket} (re-entry at N-03); a build-mode pick is build-mode.set {state on or off, scope, expires_at, card_id} (N-44 applies it, and state off ends build mode early); the GOFACTORY standing card is gofactory {card_id} (N-49, N-50, bootstrap B2); the halt and resume standing cards are control.halt and control.resume {card_id, word} (N-44 writes flag:hold, the single writer; shared/seat-contract.xml#halt-and-resume); break glass is break.glass {request, target} (one time, seat-contract.xml#break-glass); a promotion confirm is promotion.confirm {head_sha}, which N-09 reads before it merges a change to the owner-locked page assets (nodes/N-48/spec.xml#owner-confirm). This node writes no flag and acts on no effect; the tailing node does, level-triggered, so a lost frame never loses a ruling.
Close the card: N-28 writes card.done 200 on seeing the ruling; the intake does not write it (one writer per kind).

Ack: the reply to the page carries the ruling or the refusal; the page shows it as the answer's receipt (N-32 look). For a relay, the CLI prints the ruling id and the relayer's record is the ruling's by field (the owner principal plus the session label), not a separate note.
mechanism.text: Why the owner's at is the owner's act time: an answer relayed an hour later still rules at the time the owner spoke; gates compare rulings with records by cause, not by time, so the at field is for the owner's eye and the ledger.

Why words are never parsed: USERHALT and USERGO inside the words of an answer are not commands; an owner word is a whole trimmed message from an owner principal (shared/authority.xml#owner-words), which N-30 matches and delivers here as an answer on its standing card, or the Controls lever (N-42). A card about a halt has its options; the pick is the command.

sources-of-answers.source: The owner taps an option and types words on the bearings page (N-32); the page service calls Intake.Answer before it acks the browser; the watcher (N-27) delivers the same record a second time by stream and gets the same ruling back.

The owner answers in chat, on the phone, or in a terminal, and the owner, or the owner's own interactive architect session in the owner's terminal, runs coq owner answer --relay --card C-42 --pick 3 --words "owner answered in chat from the phone: went recommended" --session <label> under the owner uid (shared/seat-contract.xml#relay). The by field is the owner principal plus the label; the record is a ruling with source=relay, and the page shows it on the card so the owner sees his own answer landed. A relay may carry only none or ticket.unblock (shared/authority.xml#relayable-rulings): an owner-only card (GOFACTORY, B7 ready, break glass, build mode, promotion confirm, halt, resume) answered by relay is answer.rejected 403 not_relayable and the card stays open. A seat has no socket at all (shared/authority.xml#role-derivation), so a relay by a seat cannot reach this node.

A standing policy row's deadline passes (N-28 step 3; only relayable cards carry a deadline): the builder calls Intake.Answer with source=policy, pick=default; the ruling says so, and the page shows "defaulted by policy" on the closed card. A defaulted ruling never carries gofactory, control.halt, control.resume, break.glass, build-mode.set or promotion.confirm; step 1 refuses it 403 not_relayable even if a template asked. The owner may overturn through a fresh card when the template marks the ruling reopenable (ruling field reopenable).

An owner-initiated action on the Controls screen (N-42: hold, resume, build-mode, one-time break glass) is an answer on that lever's standing card (nodes/N-28/spec.xml#standing-cards) posted through the page service in an owner session, with the client's action id as the idempotency subject; one ruling per action id, a repeat replays. Break glass stays one time by the seat contract (a second break.glass ruling on one request id is answer.refused).

An owner word typed alone on the owner page in an owner session (shared/authority.xml#owner-words) is matched by N-30 and delivered here as an answer on the word's standing card with action_id = the owner.message id; N-30 is an allowed caller for standing cards only.
The owner CLI under the owner uid, reading the answer from its controlling terminal, with no agent harness among its ancestors (shared/authority.xml#owner-words).
The legacy answers.jsonl imported once at cut-over (nodes/N-32/spec.xml#cut-over step 3): ruled with effects [none], imported true, never routed and never an owner word.

start.text: Intake is a gRPC service inside coq.service (N-06 unit.start); it is up when the service is up. It ships dark behind intake.enabled in the service config and goes live by its own ticket with the proof: one page answer on dev produces a ruling, a second answer on the same card is refused 409, a relayed answer on dev produces a ruling with source=relay. The old answers.jsonl path stays until the cut-over step in N-32's runbook migrates it.

wait.fallback: retry 3 times (200 ms apart); then answer.rejected 400 with reason store, which the page shows as 'not recorded, try again' and keeps the answer queued locally (N-32) for its own 3 retries
retry 3 times (1, 2, 4 s) then reply unavailable 503 to the caller; the page keeps the answer queued and retries; the watcher's stream delivery is the second path

retry 3 times with the same operation key; a replay or a 409 means the ruling exists; a timeout after 3 tries replies 503 and the owner.answer record stays with no ruling, which the tick (N-06) lists every second as answers-without-ruling and re-runs step 3 for, so no answer can be persisted and never ruled
keep the last good table; the ruling is written with effects=[] and a ruling.effects.unknown 500 alert so a reader does not act on a wrong effect; the tick re-computes effects when the table reloads

waits.no-cog: The cog that could stall this node is the store. Timeout: 3 tries. Fallback: the page's local queue, the watcher's second delivery and the tick's answers-without-ruling scan. No agent sits between the owner's tap and the ruling.

retries.rule: Every store call retries 3 times with backoff then reports with a 500 or 503 record; the answers-without-ruling scan on every tick is the recovery, and it is idempotent because the ruling key is the card id.
An answer is never dropped: it is persisted before anything else, and a persisted answer is ruled by the scan within one tick of the store returning.

many-agents-at-once.readers: Any number of seats read this volume; the effects table is one file edited by one ticket at a time.
many-agents-at-once.workers: Build tickets from this node touch internal/owner/intake, the Intake proto service, tools/bearings/config/answer-effects.json and the CLI verb coq owner answer; the page, the builder and the watcher own other files.

collision.what: the owner answers one card on two devices within the same second

many-agents-at-once.collision: Two owner.answer records persist (both are his acts); step 3 commits one ruling by create-only put; the second caller gets answer.refused 409 and its device shows already answered with the winning choice. Nothing is lost and nothing is double-applied.

collision.what: the page service and the watcher deliver the same owner.answer

many-agents-at-once.collision: Same record id: persist is a no-op, step 3 returns the existing ruling; both callers get the same reply.

collision.what: a relay races the owner's own page answer

many-agents-at-once.collision: First commit wins by card id; the loser is refused with the winner attached. The page shows which one landed; if they differ, the owner sees it on the card and may re-open through a new card. The relay CLI prints the refusal and the winner so the architect never records a wrong ruling.

collision.what: a policy default and the owner's answer at the deadline second

many-agents-at-once.collision: Same rule: one wins by create-only put. A policy ruling marked reopenable lets N-28 open a fresh card for the owner's late answer, which is the "owner may overturn" rule of V17 kept honest.
Refused at start by N-06 (failure-cases.xml#duplicate-instance); within the one instance, create-only commits and idempotent persists make every call safe to repeat.

collision.what: USERHALT typed on the page while the owner pulls the Controls lever

many-agents-at-once.collision: Two answers on the halt standing card with two action ids: two rulings, both control.halt; N-44 applies the first and the second is a no-op on an already held flag.
many-agents-at-once.test: tests run two Intake clients firing the same and different answers to one card under the fake clock: exactly one ruling, every caller receives either the ruling or a 409 carrying it, the scan rules a persisted answer whose first put timed out.

permissions.runs-as: inside coq-service as the service user coq-svc (shared/authority.xml#principals); Intake is served on /run/coq/store.sock
permissions.callers: N-32 the page service (source page via tap with the session's role, source controls for the N-42 lever, source imported during the cut-over import); N-27 the watcher (second delivery of an answer already persisted, source as stored); N-30 the inbox (source page via message, standing cards only); N-28 the card builder (source policy, relayable cards only); the owner CLI under the owner uid (source cli, or relay with --relay). Any other caller, or a listed caller with a source not its own, is answer.rejected 403 caller_not_allowed.
permissions.may-not: a seat has no socket and can never call Intake.Answer; a pod never reaches the socket (D23: no secret access, host-only socket); this node never writes a flag entity (N-44 is the single writer)
permissions.identity: the caller's principal, node and role come from SO_PEERCRED (shared/authority.xml#role-derivation); the owner's role on the page comes from the session N-32 proved (nodes/N-32/spec.xml#web-security); COQ_SEAT is diagnostic only and never authority

runbook.op: coq owner answer --relay --card C-42 --pick 3 --words "<the owner's words, quoted>"; the CLI prints the ruling id or the refusal with the winner; the architect never writes answers.jsonl by hand again

op.name: an answer shows as not recorded on the page

runbook.op: the page retried 3 times and the store was down; check coq.service (N-06 runbook); the queued answer in the browser posts itself when the page reconnects; the watcher's stream delivery is the backstop
coq owner import-answers --file ~/.bearings/coq-stable/answers.jsonl --dry-run, then --yes; refuses if any id already exists unless --skip-existing
store retention by N-45; journal by tools/bearings/bin/cleanup-journal.sh; legacy files by tools/bearings/bin/cleanup-tier.sh --legacy
runbook.cost: One more gRPC service and a rule table to keep in step with the card templates (make lint checks every template row has an effects row or none).

a relayed answer recorded by hand: "owner answered in chat from the phone: went recommended"
post the ruling as a record before prompting; an unrecorded ruling cost PR 156 a rework
